chapter: Hearing Louis and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Following Louis's career and the Heebie-Jeebies record
summary: After the parade everybody in Baton Rouge talked of Louis; Joe's first strong record memory is Heebie-Jeebies, around 1926.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But everybody, just all we could talk about was Louis Armstrong. We called him Louis. And I said, 'Well, I'm going to play with that guy one of these days.'
I'm going to get to that, naturally, obviously, later on. That's going to be probably a tape in itself. But did you follow Louis' career as he went along?
Yeah. That's when I really started listening to records. That's when I remember. Then Louis came out... Right after that he started coming out with a record like 'Cornet Chop Suey'...
Well, wait a minute. First he would have gone up to join Joe Oliver's band, which was 1923 or something...
Yeah, then he left New Orleans. I never seen him no more.
Did you ever hear Joe Oliver's records with Louis on them?
I really can't remember. I can't say. The first record I really remember that really made an impression on me with Louis was "Heebie-Jeebies."
Yeah. Now, that was long after this, naturally.
I'm trying to think when the Hot Fives were recorded. '26 or something like that?
That's right. That's when Ory left with... When I got to Los Angeles in '26, Ory had just left here and went to Chicago. Because Ory had been living here in Los Angeles.
